pr_title: vo_libmpv: make sure kill_cb is finished before freeing update_lock and update_cond
pr_body:
The atomic variable in_use is set to 0 before kill_cb is called, but the code
did not wait for the invocation of the callback, which caused accessing an
already destroyed mutex/conditonal and deadlocks when exiting the simple SDL
example.

Fixes #6531.

I agree that my changes can be relicensed to LGPL 2.1 or later.
pr_comments: `kill_cb` is used to wake up `mpv_render_context_free` when vo is destroyed, but the [`uninit`](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/blob/6e4971f69738056376e0a0c22fb59bb32a0092f9/video/out/vo_libmpv.c#L704) also does this. Can we resolve the issue by removing `kill_cb`?

issue_context.title: libmpv: race condition using simple SDL example at shutdown
issue_context.body:

git master, linux

### Reproduction steps

1. Compile the SDL example: gcc -o main main.c \`pkg-config --libs --cflags mpv sdl2\` -std=c99
2. Run valgrind --tool=drd --show-confl-seg=no --trace-cond=yes  ./main av://lavfi:testsrc
3. Close the window when the video is already running

No "condition variable has not been initialized" or "Mutex not locked" errors.

### Comments

The conditinal and mutex which is referenced by thread 2 is already destroyed by thread 1.

It is possible that you have to try 3-4 times to hit this with valgrind.

The issue seems realtively harmless but I suspect this is the root cause of some hangs I am seeing occasionally with libmpv.

review_comments: the loop will exit if `had_kill` is `true`. is `had_update` useless?

a corner case where `had_kill == true && had_update == false` causes waiting infinitely, because there is no more `update` to wake it up when `had_kill == true`. try adding `mp_sleep_us(1000000);` after this line to reproduce the issue. removing `had_update` can fix it.
